Definition: from G1772 and G1416; to sink (by implication, wrap (compare G1746) on, i.e. (figuratively) sneak:--creep.
BiblicalUsage: Paul warns of men who creep into houses and lead captive silly women laden with sins in 2 Timothy 3:6 — false teachers who do not knock at the front door but slip in quietly.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe error rarely announces itself — it creeps in, and the defence is a household that knows the truth well enough to spot a stranger.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
